text: Comparative research has shown that those who were buried at Hrísbrú were significantly shorter than other Icelanders from the colonization period (AD 870-930). Previous research has shown that in the Viking Age, Icelanders were on average taller than people from Norway. The height of people is usually determined by diet, health, and genetics. According to the skeletal evidence, the people at Hrísbrú lived under harsh conditions. The isotope analysis provides clear evidence that the diet of the people of Hrísbrú was made up of 1/3 marine foods. This suggests that the utilization of marine resources was more common than has previously been thought and that Icelanders may have begun to fish and collect shellfish soon after the initial settlement.
